first_impression.reaction: Googled 'best time to get married in bali' while comparing planners. Expected a 'dry season is perfect!' puff piece. Instead the first line is 'There is no single right time to get married in Bali.' and the wet season is sourced to Smartraveller and BMKG. Jumped to the FAQ, then the dates. Real dates, real caveats. But a booking CTA shows up before I've seen any evidence, and there's not one rainfall figure, price difference or word on how Wedded Wonderland gets paid.

journey.quote: There is no single right time to get married in Bali.
journey.reaction: Good. Nobody's pretending one month is magic. Trade-offs, not a sales line.

journey.quote: Smartraveller places Indonesia's wet season usually around October to April, and Bali's own climate station publishes a fresh forecast of each season's start every year.
journey.reaction: Named sources, government ones. I can check both. That's the standard I want.

journey.quote: Once you have two or three months in mind, talk to Wedded Concierge about your dates and turn them into dates a venue can hold.
journey.reaction: A sales link before I've even read the month-by-month. Let me get through the evidence first.

journey.section: The dry months, May to September
journey.quote: Dry is not the same as rainless. Every outdoor ceremony in Bali still needs a covered backup, whatever the month.
journey.reaction: Honest. Most sites sell July as guaranteed sunshine. This is the catch said up front.

journey.quote: Through these months, weather can change quickly and heavy rain can disrupt roads and transport.
journey.reaction: Fine, but how wet? Average rainfall per month, rainy days, anything. A month-by-month guide with zero numbers on the actual weather is thin.

journey.section: How to read BMKG's seasonal forecast for your year
journey.quote: A day under 5 mm is very light rain, 5 to 20 mm light, 20 to 50 mm moderate, 50 to 100 mm heavy and over 100 mm very heavy.
journey.reaction: Useful scale. Now show me where each month typically sits on it.

journey.section: How to read BMKG's seasonal forecast for your year
journey.quote: Treat any single year's figures as that year's weather, not as a guide to yours, and check the outlook again three months before the wedding.
journey.reaction: Which figures? The page hasn't shown me any. Feels like a reason not to give numbers.

journey.quote: Idul Fitri is confirmed by a later ministerial decision, so hold those dates loosely.
journey.reaction: Admits the date can move. That's the kind of detail I'd only otherwise find on Reddit after the fact.

journey.quote: If you move indoors or change the date, how do deposits and payments carry across, and what does the contract say in writing?
journey.reaction: Exactly the question I got burned on last time. Sharp list.

journey.section: Chapels and covered spaces, as each venue describes them
journey.quote: The St. Regis Bali Resort has the Cloud Nine Chapel on its beachfront, with Swarovski crystal chandeliers and ocean views, a pond and cascading steps, and a wooden terrace beyond for canapés and drinks.
journey.reaction: Brochure copy. No capacity, no cost. Chandeliers don't help me pick a month.

journey.section: Chapels and covered spaces, as each venue describes them
journey.quote: Notice the capacities. A chapel for 70 and a lawn for 250 suit very different guest lists, and the covered space needs to hold everyone, not only the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Practical. Catches the trick where the 'rain plan' only seats half the guests.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so the covered plan and the weather call are settled before the deposit is paid.
journey.reaction: In writing is right. But what does the Advisor cost and who pays them?

journey.section: Larger guest lists travelling from Australia
journey.quote: July, September, October and November have no 2027 national holidays, which keeps supplier and travel planning simple.
journey.reaction: Holidays are only half of it. Does a July date cost more than November? Do Aussie school holidays push up flights? Nothing on price by season.

journey.quote: You move to the covered space agreed in your contract.

journey.section: Plan your month with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, and plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you.
journey.reaction: Payments go through you. So do you take a cut from the venue? What's the fee? Same silence as every planner site.

unanswered_questions: What does each month actually look like in numbers: typical rainfall in mm or rainy days, sourced and dated?
Do venue or package prices differ between dry and wet season, and by how much?
Do Australian school holidays line up with the dry months and push up guest flight and room costs?
Is there any cost to holding a covered backup space, or is it included?
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee calculated, and what's a realistic 'from AUD' figure? (deferred business detail)
Do you take commissions or mark-ups from venues or suppliers, and will you disclose them? (deferred business detail)
Show me a real Bali wedding you've planned, with its month, the weather on the day and the actual budget. (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Once you have two or three months in mind, talk to Wedded Concierge about your dates and turn them into dates a venue can hold.
turn_offs_found.why: CTA before any evidence; it sits right after the takeaways, before the month-by-month.

turn_offs_found.quote: Through these months, weather can change quickly and heavy rain can disrupt roads and transport.
turn_offs_found.why: A weather guide with no weather figures. Without numbers I can't compare months myself.

turn_offs_found.quote: The St. Regis Bali Resort has the Cloud Nine Chapel on its beachfront, with Swarovski crystal chandeliers and ocean views, a pond and cascading steps, and a wooden terrace beyond for canapés and drinks.
turn_offs_found.why: Decorative description instead of the capacity number the page itself tells me to check.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, and plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you.
turn_offs_found.why: Money flows through the planner but there's no fee model or commission disclosure.

turn_offs_found.quote: For more ideas, browse our digital wedding magazines.
turn_offs_found.why: Mood boards, not proof. I want a real wedding with a real budget.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the March 2027 breakdown (Nyepi plus Idul Fitri) and the 'covered space must hold everyone' point
Our Reddit thread: the venue questions list (weather call deadline, deposits if you move indoors) and the BMKG rain bands

cta_reaction.why: Sourced, dated, honest about rain and moving holiday dates, so trust is decent. But no rainfall numbers, no price difference by season and nothing on fees or commissions. I'd email those questions before booking a call.

top_3_changes: Add sourced, dated monthly rainfall figures (mm or rainy days) to the month-by-month section, or say plainly that none are published and why.
Add a cost-by-season signal: whether venue or package pricing changes dry versus wet, and a note on Australian school holidays and flights, with 'not published' where no source exists.
Move the first Concierge CTA below the month-by-month, and next to the closing CTA state how the fee works and whether supplier commissions apply (deferred business detail).

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft

No invented brand facts; fees, commissions and real weddings listed as deferred unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

Business details (fees, commissions, real weddings) are deferred; voiced as unanswered questions only.
